result.classification: Common-Controls v6 activation-context manifest missing from Rust unit-test executable

sidecar_staging.note: -SkipGo is insufficient in a clean worktree because tauri-build requires the cmuxd-remote externalBin resource too.

loader_failure.result: both exit -1073741511 (0xc0000139) before Rust test enumeration

working_binary.runtime_observation: process remained alive and its loaded-module list contained the WinSxS Common-Controls v6 comctl32.dll

test_manifest.observation: c101008c: image did not contain a resource section

base_dll.observation: base Common-Controls v5.82 does not export TaskDialogIndirect

desktop_manifest.observation: resource #1 requests Microsoft.Windows.Common-Controls version 6.0.0.0, processorArchitecture *, publicKeyToken 6595b64144ccf1df, language *

source_chain.fact: cmux-desktop links tauri with the wry runtime and tauri-plugin-dialog; both Windows implementations can reference TaskDialogIndirect
the build script only calls tauri_build::build()
the default Tauri manifest requests Microsoft.Windows.Common-Controls v6
Tauri assigns that manifest to tauri-winres and calls WindowsResource::compile
because this crate has src/main.rs, compile emits cargo:rustc-link-arg-bins for the resource object, so the application bin receives it but the lib unit-test harness does not
the Windows dialog implementations reference TaskDialogIndirect

excluded_causes.system_runtime_mismatch: not a corrupt or obsolete runtime: the installed WinSxS v6 DLL exports the symbol and is loaded by the manifested desktop binary
excluded_causes.webview2_or_windows_sdk: not the missing import: the sole observed unresolved direct import is comctl32.dll!TaskDialogIndirect; no WebView2Loader failure occurs
excluded_causes.sidecar_artifact: not causal: failure occurs in the Windows PE loader before Rust main/test enumeration, after both required sidecars are staged
excluded_causes.native_tls_or_schannel: not causal: the missing entrypoint belongs to comctl32, not secur32/crypt32/schannel
excluded_causes.tauri_test_harness: not a Rust harness assertion: direct --list fails before the harness starts; Tauri's bin-only resource-linking behavior is the build-time trigger
excluded_causes.path_dll_shadowing: not observed: no local comctl32.dll is staged; the unmanifested loader resolves the system base DLL while the normal binary activates the WinSxS v6 assembly

minimal_fix_plan.red_test: On Windows, stage both sidecars, run cargo test -p cmux-desktop --lib --no-run, locate the emitted cmux_desktop_lib-*.exe, assert mt.exe can extract resource #1 and that it names Microsoft.Windows.Common-Controls version 6.0.0.0; then run the executable with --list and require exit 0.
minimal_fix_plan.implementation: In apps/desktop/src-tauri/build.rs on MSVC Windows, add the Common-Controls v6 linker manifest dependency for test targets (cargo:rustc-link-arg-tests=/MANIFESTDEPENDENCY:type='win32' name='Microsoft.Windows.Common-Controls' version='6.0.0.0' processorArchitecture='*' publicKeyToken='6595b64144ccf1df' language='*'). Keep tauri_build::build() for the normal application resources.
minimal_fix_plan.fallback_if_unit_lib_test_is_not_classif: Generate a tiny Common-Controls v6 .manifest/.rc resource in OUT_DIR and explicitly link its compiled .res into the lib unit-test harness, or move desktop unit-testable logic into a non-Tauri crate; do not copy or preload a comctl32.dll.
minimal_fix_plan.simplification: Prefer the single /MANIFESTDEPENDENCY test-target linker argument over duplicating the entire Tauri icon/version resource pipeline.

local_pe_checks: mt.exe extracts resource #1 from the test executable
cargo build -p cmux-desktop passes and its existing manifest remains unchanged
hosted_windows_ci: stage real CLI and Go sidecars with scripts/desktop/stage-sidecars.ps1
run the PE manifest/import assertions on the emitted test executable
record exact test executable exit code and archive extracted test manifest as evidence
